title: Building a reference
intent: formative · pattern sequential-process · a Harvard web reference, built in order
statement: Build a Harvard reference for a website, one element at a time — each element doing one job, so a reader can trace your exact source.

stage.intro: A reference has five jobs: who (author), when (year), what (title), where (source) and, for the web, when you read it (access date).

steps.title: What a reference must do
steps.text: A reference lets a reader find your exact source. Build it in order, each element doing one job.

steps.title: Author — who
steps.text: Surname, then initial: “Smith, J.” With no author, you would use the organisation instead.

steps.title: Year — when
steps.text: The date of publication, in round brackets: “(2021)”. With no date, you would write “(no date)”.

steps.title: Title — what
steps.text: The title of the work, italicised for a standalone source: “Renewable futures.”

steps.title: Source — where
steps.text: For a website, the full address after “Available at:” so the reader can go straight to it.

steps.title: Access date — when you read it
steps.text: Web pages change, so record the date you saw it: “(Accessed: 3 October 2025).”

steps.title: A complete reference
steps.text: Every element, in order, punctuated consistently — a reader can now trace the source exactly. The same discipline underlies every citation style.
